content.title: Arkansas basketball survives Ole Miss, advances to SEC Tournament Championship
content.text: Updated March 14, 2026, 5:18 p.m. CTNASHVILLE, Tenn. — It’s been 26 years since Arkansas basketball won its first-and-only SEC Tournament Championship. The Hogs are one victory away from ending that drought. The No. 3-seed Razorbacks (25-8) beat the No. 15 Rebels (15-20) 93-90 in overtime during the semifinals on Saturday, March 14. The Razorbacks blew a seven-point lead in the final 2:38 of regulation and went 2 for 6 from the free-throw line in the final minute of overtime, but they found a way to win with Darius Acuff Jr. scoring five of their final six points. Two slithering layups in the extra period proved to be the difference.The victory hands Arkansas a date with Vanderbilt in the championship after the Commodores stunned No. 1-seed Florida on the other side of the bracket. Arkansas used a furious pace right from tipoff to build an early advantage. Four of the Hogs’ first five baskets were dunks, and they tried to get out and run on nearly every miss from the Rebels. A Malique Ewin put-back layup followed an alley-oop from Meleek Thomas to Trevon Brazile, and Arkansas led 23-12 with 10:45 remaining. It felt like the game was slipping away from Ole Miss, but the Rebels started to generate good offense through Malik Dia, and that limited the Razorbacks’ transition opportunities. Dia had 10 of his 16 points in the first half, and a bad foul by Nick Pringle in the final seconds gave Patton Pinkins three free throws. He converted them all, and Arkansas’ lead dwindled to 37-36 at halftime. Neither team created any separation coming out of the locker room. There were 10 lead changes within the first 10 minutes, and the game was tied 58-58 with 9:14 remaining.That’s when Arkansas landed the first punch of the second half with a 10-0 run across 2:16. However, the Razorbacks failed to score in a 2:31 stretch that lasted until there were 5.8 seconds remaining, allowing Ole Miss to rally and force overtime. AJ Storr tied the game with a coast-to-coast layup on the Rebels’ final possession. Storr nearly willed Ole Miss to a victory by himself. He scored nine points in overtime, but he missed a potential game-winning triple with less than 10 seconds remaining. He finished with 24 points.The Southwest Times Record provided live updates throughout the game. Our recap is below. Watch Arkansas basketball vs Ole Miss in SEC TournamentArkansas basketball vs Ole Miss live score updatesSecond Half End of Regulation: Arkansas 79, Ole Miss 79The Razorbacks blew a seven-point lead with 2:38 remaining. Meleek Thomas missed a free throw with five seconds on the clock that woudl have pushed the lead to three. AJ Storr capitalized with a game-tying layup at the other end, and the Rebels' dream is still alive. Arkansas leads 74-69, 3:12All of a sudden, Arkansas can't grab a rebound. The Hogs led by 10 just a couple minutes ago, but Ole Miss is back within striking distance thanks to 3s and second-chance points. Dariuys Acuff Jr. provided a clutch basket while getting fouled to take us into the final media timeout of the game. Arkansas leads 64-58, 7:04The Hogs are in the midst of a 6-0 run with back-to-back dunks by Malique Ewin on their last two possessions. Both baskets were set up by stout defense from Billy Richmond III at the other end. Darius Acuff Jr. is headed to the free-throw line after the current media timeout. This feels like a chance for Arkansas to land a knockout punch, something the Razorbacks have struggle with away from Bud Walton Arena all season. Arkansas leads 58-55, 9:47Meleek Thomas is cooking with 20 points on 7 for 12 shooting with four 3-pointers. Still, Arkansas can't get enough stops to put the Rebels away. Ole Miss is shooting 52.9% from the field in the second period. Ole Miss leads 47-44, 15:31The Rebels are playing terrific defense since coming out of the locker room. Arkansas is 1 for 5 and Darius Acuff Jr. has all seven of his team's points, doing most of his damage from the free-throw line. On the other end, the Rebels are 5 for 8 as they continue to work through Malik Dia.First Half HALF: Arkansas 37, Ole Miss 36The Rebels closed the period with a 6-0 run, largely thanks to a dumb foul by Nick Pringle in the final second that gave Patton Pinkins three free throws. Arkansas is shooting 47.1% from the floor and struggling a bit in half-court sets. But when the Hogs get stops, they are dominating with 15 fastbreak points. Meelek Thomas has 12, Trevon Brazile has 11 while Nick Pringle, Dariys Acuff Jr. and Malique Ewin all have four. Arkansas leads 35-28, 3:32Ole Miss cut it to one, but Arkansas strung together some stops and responded with a 6-0 run. Chris Beard calls a timeout after a steal and layup by Darius Acuff Jr., but it's Meleek Thomas leading the offense right now with 12 points and three assists. Arkansas leads 27-23, 7:00Malik Dia is starting to get going for Ole Miss, and the Rebels have 4 of their last 5 shots. They've trimmed the deficit to four at the under-eight media timeout. Darius Acuff Jr. has the most recent Arkansas basket for his first points of the day. Arkansas leads 21-12, 10:56The Razorbacks are playing with incredible pace and Ole Miss looks like this is its fourth game in as many days. Fantastic starts for Meleek Thomas and Trevon Brazile, who have eight and nine points, respectively. Arkansas is shooting 60% and leads by nine without a single point from Darius Acuff Jr. Arkansas leads 10-7, 14:03Four of the Razorbacks' first five baskets have been dunks. Darius Acuff Jr. hasn't had a crisp start with two turnovers and two missed shots, but he does have three rebounds and two assists. Ole Miss is looking to go right at Trevon Brazile through Malik Dia, but Braziel has held his own in the early minutes.Pregame No changes to Arkansas basketball's starting lineupDarius Acuff Jr., Meleek Thomas, Billy Richmond III, Trevon Brazile and Nick Pringle will be the first five for John Calipari's squad as it tries to halt the tournament's Cinderella. Vanderbilt whoops Florida in other semifinalIt's a stunner as the Commodores beat the Gators 91-74 to advance to the SEC Tournament Championship. The Gators might have just lost their grasp on a No. 1 seed at the NCAA Tournament, too. The winer of Arkansas and Ole Miss will face Vanderbilt tomorrow afternoon.What time does Arkansas vs Ole Miss start?Date: Saturday, March 14Time: 2:30 p.m. CT Where: Bridgestone Arena in Nashville, Tenn.What TV channel is Arkansas vs Ole Miss on today? TV Channel: ESPNLivestream: Fubo (free trial), ESPN+How to watch online: Fubo (Free trial), ESPN+ (here's how to stream it live)Arkansas vs Ole Miss predictionOle Miss is playing its best basketball of the season, but the Rebels will finally run out of gas in their fourth game in as many days. Look for Meleek Thomas to have a strong game and Darius Acuff Jr. to continue his torrid close to the year.
